**Test image key features:**
- Single large oval/elliptical lesion on a cauliflower leaf
- Deeply necrotic, collapsed interior tissue — dark brown/black
- Prominent blackened vein structures visible within the lesion
- Surrounding tissue shows clear yellowing/chlorosis

**Reference comparison:**
- **Bacterial Soft Rot** (PlantWild_18, PlantWild_27): Both showed decay on cauliflower curd/head — no leaf lesions, very different
- **Alternaria Leaf Spot** (PlantWild_24, PlantWild_35): Both showed sporulation/browning on the head — no leaf lesions
- **Black Rot** (Cauliflower_1006, 1057, 1061): Showed leaf yellowing and some spots; Cauliflower_1061 showed leaf-level chlorosis, vein highlighting consistent with vascular infection
- **Downy Mildew** (Cauliflower_1012): Showed leaf with multiple necrotic brown lesions — similar in being leaf-level damage

**Decision:** The most diagnostic feature in the test image is the **blackened vein structures** visible inside the lesion combined with the surrounding yellowing/chlorosis — these are hallmarks of Black Rot (Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris), which colonizes the vascular system and causes xylem blackening. The Downy Mildew reference was the only one showing leaf-level damage, but none of its characteristic features (yellow patches, downy sporulation) match. The vein blackening and chlorosis pattern is most consistent with Black Rot at an advanced stage.
